props.text: Membrane washing, DWR reactivation & field sizing

props.html: Most shells sent to our bench as "leaking" are simply saturated with skin oils blocking vapour transport. Regular gentle washing doubles laminate lifespan.

items.a: Wash every 10 to 12 days of active mountain use at 40°C using liquid, fragrance-free technical detergent with zero fabric softeners, optical brighteners, or powdered soap.
items.q: How often should I wash a 3-layer ePTFE storm shell?

items.a: After rinsing twice, tumble dry on medium-warm (60°C) for 25 minutes. Gentle heat re-aligns the branched hydrocarbon polymers so sleet beads cleanly off the 70D face.
items.q: How do I reactivate the fluorocarbon-free C0 DWR bead at home?

items.a: Lyngen shells use an articulated alpine cut sized to fit comfortably over a base layer and midweight fleece or light active hoody, while allowing a high-loft belay parka over the outside.
items.q: Are Lyngen shells cut for belay insulation underneath or over top?

items.a: Never machine-wash or spin-dry UHMWPE composite packs. Rinse salt and mud out with lukewarm water and a soft brush, then hang upside-down in shade.
items.q: Can woven Dyneema® packs go in a washing machine?

props.text: Free ultrasonic seam repair for the life of the shell

props.html: The cleanest expedition jacket is the one still climbing in its twelfth winter. Our Tromsø harbour bench repairs every batch-numbered SKARVEN piece regardless of original owner.
Every incoming shell or pack passes through three bench stations within five working days of reaching Tromsø.
